newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.N. protests Serb harassment of Bosnian Moslems.
newsitem.headline: U.N. protests Serb harassment of Bosnian Moslems.

text.p: Bosnian Serbs have carried out a systematic campaign of harrassment against Moslems living in the town of Teslic over the past two months and local police have failed to intervene, a U.N. spokesman said on Wednesday.
"The United Nations is disturbed by a two-month upsurge in harassment and attacks against the remaining Moslem population of Teslic," U.N. spokesman Alexander Ivanko said in Sarajevo.

"They include attacks with petrol bombs, grenades and other explosives, vandalism, arson, stealing and killing of cattle, verbal and telephone threats...On Monday, a number of unoccupied houses belonging to Moslems were set on fire."
About 1,860 Moslems still reside in Serb-controlled Teslic in north-central Bosnia, which is a part of that 49 per cent of the country known as Republika Srpska.
Ivanko said the presence of U.N. police monitors in the area was cited by the remaining Moslems as one of their few incentives to stay in their homes.
"The local police have the ability to stop the harassment of Moslems since the perpetrators are well-known in Teslic," the U.N. spokesman added.
"This situation when minorities are pressured to leave Republika Srpska should not be allowed to continue."
